subject.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists

question: Should OpenClaw accept pre-auth delivery of blocked DM content and automatic managed-hook activation, and should sender grouping reuse the existing named access-group contract or introduce a new per-entry role model?
rationale: The decision changes a public plugin hook, blocked-message confidentiality, hook activation defaults, channel config shapes, prompt metadata, and the meaning of access groups; code review cannot choose those permanent product and security contracts safely.

options.title: Narrow and reuse the canonical contract
options.body: Keep the useful pre-auth workflow, replace per-channel `{number, group}` roles with shared access-group references, and require explicit activation unless a separate approved policy says otherwise.

options.title: Approve the new role model
options.body: Explicitly adopt the six fixed per-sender roles and automatic trusted-hook activation as new supported contracts, with upgrade documentation and compatibility tests.

options.title: Split the feature
options.body: Separate pre-auth observation from sender grouping so each security and API contract can be reviewed and landed independently.

recommendation.title: Narrow and reuse the canonical contract
recommendation.body: Keep the useful pre-auth workflow, replace per-channel `{number, group}` roles with shared access-group references, and require explicit activation unless a separate approved policy says otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical access-group contract was introduced through their merged work, making them the strongest available owner for deciding whether it should remain the single model.
